anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: All three facts moved from fails to holds, and Before held none of them, so nothing was lost. The assess and dispatch facts moved because After's pick lifecycle step persists work_started true, deletes the saved note and nulls reject before the review POST or the dispatch; Before did none of this. The dispatch fact also needed the remedy-first derived AC (instead/replaces, builds, base evidence, P1, test/index.test.js) and the statement that Claude Code gets the same pack verbatim, both of which After has. The needs fact moved because After renders Problem 1 under the three headings with overrule 1 among the choices and scopes later reviews to carried closure-only P1 with no repeated whole-PR approach judgment. Before used a prose paragraph, offered no overrule and said a new session would review the whole diff. Three places hold only by inference and are worth tightening. First, the pi report says the test "failed with: missing source fixture", which reads close to an invented test failure; wording such as "the command reported a missing source fixture before the test could run" would be safer. Second, nothing at the stuck exit says the course stays deliver and P1 stays open. The stray "with target file" in D3 step 1 and the Claude Code report omitting the scoped command it ran are minor and could be cleaned up.

The needs fact holds on a lenient reading, and three wording gaps make it fragile: After never states the exit as the literal `stuck - needs source fixture`, never says course deliver and P1 are retained in saved state, and conveys the no-round charge only indirectly ("falls under the failed-needs round-charge exception", "not a source-changing repair round").
